angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 257,409 km at 20.39 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 49.0544 +/- 0.0236 mas (same row, RUWE 1.39): 20.39 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.37 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Dai et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6255 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..101D/abstract): 257,409 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.353 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Dai et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6255 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..101D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3421 +/- 70 K from Dai et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6255 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..101D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dai et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6255 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..101D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6255.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.849, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, G 189-1: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-6255 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.14 dex, from Dai et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..101D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-6255 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.77344, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
